findings: README describes extent/block hash candidate discovery and optional Linux FIDEDUPERANGE data sharing. This is extent storage dedup, not perceptual matching or file removal. No mutating ioctl or upstream command executed.

tests.c contains3 MU_TEST cases: zero block, block_len boundaries and rename helper. Test inventory path count1 did not mean one test. Rename case relies on executable pathname existence to simulate hardlink handling; zero test passesNULL in final case rather than modified block. Needs helper source before interpreting adequacy.

dedupe.h caps120 total extents (source plus119 destinations), explicit queued/in-progress/completed ownership lists, per-request returned byte counts/status. Important transferable distinction: bytes processed, bytes shared, and full-file duplicate identity are different results.

dedupe.c only upper-clamps max_extents before subtracting1; zero/one preconditions not checked locally. Call-site reachability remains unreviewed. Kernel-success zero-byte/status0 response would requeue unchanged with no progress guard in this loop; actual kernel contract and callers unverified, so conditional observation rather than reproduced kernel defect.

On first destinationEINVAL with fs_blocksize0, code queries block size (fallback4096) and retries aligned length; alignment state is static global. Per-filesystem/multithread context needs caller review. Source bitmask alignment assumes power-of-two block size. No Linux native runtime/build/test qualification on current macOS host.

file_scan.c only selected lines540..595 and735..855 read. process_blocks zero test uses buffer->buf+dl_offset unchanged in every iteration while actual process_block uses buffer->buf+i*blocksize. Original C-function harness zero/data hashes0 instead expected1; data/zero hashes2 instead expected1. Confirms intra-buffer zero-filter bug under synthetic two-block inputs; full scan reachability/default options still need caller review.

is_file_renamed compares strings then only lstat old path existence, not inode identity; lstat anyerror returns true. Existing oldpath test does not prove alias identity. is_block_zeroed first int load assumes at least4byte aligned/readable buffer; full-block caller inspected, input constraints pending.

Whole csum-test.c read: manual print-and-compare checksum utility, not automatic oracle. Empty file returns success without digest; -b uses atoi without local positive bound, buf_len0 can lead immediateEOF behavior with no bytes processed; read one-shot accepts short positive read. No command/runtime exercised.

Read file_scan.c1..270 and900..1170; CLI selected135..185/355..400. fill_buffer resets dl_offset0 before normal block processing; csum_whole_file calls process_blocks directly after each fill. Thus constant first-block zero check is not corrected by outer-loop offset movement. Source path reachable when do_block_hash and skip_zeroes both true with non-faked multi-block buffer.

Whole opt.c/h establish defaults skip_zeroes=false and do_block_hash=false. Zero-filter defect is opt-in combination (CLI partial option enables block hashing, skip-zeroes enables zero filter), not default extent-hash path. Existing control proves local block hash omission; no filesystem-wide candidate count/performance claim.

Scanning allocates8MiB buffer per worker plus block array filesize/blocksize+1 even when do_block_hash false; wholefile checksum includes processed bytes regardless zero-filter. Missing block candidates do not by themselves prove wrong extent/fullfile digests or corrupt ioctl output. File-size change check compares total processed with previously recorded filesize; same-size mutation/identity needs remaining source.

Completed whole file_scan.c read. Child directory statx validity uses !(st.stx_mask | STATX_BASIC_STATS), unlike top-level/helper AND. Nonzero requested mask means OR cannot detect absent returned fields; this is expression-level defect, no Linux statx scenario reproduced. Regular children with parent_checked bypass per-file filesystem identity check; bind-mounted file edge case untested.

__scan_file acquires dbfile_lock and begins transaction, then dbfile_rename_file failure returns0 without abort/unlock on this branch. Source-level cleanup defect pending verification of lock implementation/caller error injection. begin/remove-hashes/commit results also not consistently handled in enqueue stage.

Scan reuse compares cached inode/subvolume,size,mtime and old-path-existence; worker later opens pathname and fiemaps without visible fstat identity revalidation against captured inode/mtime. End check only processed-size equality; same-size replacement/mutation is not excluded by this file. Full dbfile/filerec+kernel race guarantees need review.

Whole scan implementation has no final image-perceptual operation or content-byte equality oracle before grouping; it computes checksums and stores extent/block/fullfile candidates. Empty regular files skipped intentionally. Per-file open/read failures mostly log and returnvoid; aggregate incomplete-scan status propagation requires thread/CLI review.

dbfile.c selected helpers confirm dbfile_lock/unlock directly wrap one GMutex; dbfile_rename_file returns SQLite bind/step errors and has only statement-reset cleanup, no mutex unlock/transaction abort. This supports source-level lost-lock branch in __scan_file; not reproduced with real SQLite/GLib worker. Whole dbfile source not yet read.

Whole threads.c/h read: free_pool waits for all queued work then frees registered resources; callback API has no result/error aggregation field. register_cleanup uses calloc/realloc results without null checks. This layer waits but does not qualify per-file scan completion. CLI status propagation still needs full read.

Whole csum.c/h read:16-byte XXH128/XXH3 checksum, not SHA256 despite old csum-test commentary comparison example. Digest stores low/high64 via uint64 casts (native endian/alignment); persistent cross-endian/unaligned caller compatibility unverified. State calloc/createState/reset/update statuses unchecked. Hash candidates require separate byte/kernel comparison guarantee before exact duplicate claim.

Whole CLI source read. Original main with successful parse and stub dbfile_open_handleNULL returns0 in compiled isolated harness: ret remains parse result. Confirms control-flow false-success for database-open failure; no real DB dependency qualification.

process_duplicates and __process_duplicates returnvoid, local load/search errors jump cleanup then caller may still increment/persist dedupe_seq when run_dedupe true; sync-config status ignored there. Worker scan failures have no return channel and CLI scan status reflects enumeration/config only. Source-level failure-accounting gaps, no mutating dedupe run.

fdupes mode processes groups only on blank separator; EOF returns without flushing final group. Input getline path encoding is newline-delimited, so newline filenames unsupported there. Thread counts use strtoul with no endptr/range checks before unsigned narrowing. Options --help relies execlp man success and may return if exec fails. Further focused controls optional.

Whole run_dedupe.c/h read. Main regular new_dedupe_ctxt caller asserts duplicate count>=2 before context creation; fdupes caller supplies120. Earlier local0/1 precondition issue is not reached by these inspected callers. No standalone API misuse runtime claim.

dedupe_extent_list resets non-ENOMEM errors to0; dedupe_worker discards extent_dedupe_worker return including ENOMEM. dedupe_results void cannot return worker failures to CLI. push_extents frees its local GError and returns1; caller dereferences separate err pointer initializedNULL on that error branch. Source-level enqueue-failure null-deref path, not injected yet.

FIDEDUPERANGE per-destination DIFFERS is printed as data changed; source relies on kernel result rather than assuming hash equality authorizes successful sharing. Kernel/runtime contract not executed. User-visible print_dupes_table identical label remains stronger than hashes alone without independent verification.

Original process_fdupes isolated control confirms EOF group omission:2 paths ending one newline produce0 groups; sameinput plus blank separator produces1 group. Zero real paths/files/ioctls touched. Final successful exit does not indicate final group was processed.

Whole filerec.c/h read: descriptor refcounts guarded by one mutex; per-operation open-once tokens keyed by filerec pointer. filerec holds database fileid/size/path, no expected device/inode/mtime field, open has no fstat/O_NOFOLLOW identity verification. Single-thread original-function temp-file control opens replacement inode/contentB successfully after originalA replaced; demonstrates pathname identity gap, not unsafe kernel sharing.

fdupes add_file_fdupes uses statx inode as fileid and filerec_new inserts without existing-record check; duplicate path/hardlink inode may hit duplicate-tree abort. This is source-level hypothesis until focused tree/hardlink control. General DB fileid path is separate.

Whole scan header fixes blocksize allowed4KiB..1MiB, default128KiB; earlier 4byte control exercises function logic but is below accepted CLI blocksize. Need same test at accepted4096 to qualify normal settings. FIEMAP_SKIP_FLAGS intentionally inline/unwritten only; empty-file skipping not suitable to copy as universal file-duplicate coverage.

Follow-up original-function zero-filter control rerun at CLI-accepted4096-byte blocksize with8192-byte malloc-aligned buffer reproduces same result: zero/data hashes0 and data/zero hashes2, both consume8192; expected onehash each. This removes small-block precondition uncertainty from earlier4byte synthetic control, while full Linux scan/ioctl remains unrun.

Whole FIEMAP helpers read. get_extent header promises covering extent but implementation checks only extent end>=requested offset, not start<=offset. Original synthetic C control asks hole0 with extent4096..8192 and returns extent4096 (not covering). Caller hole-handling implications require integration; not claim corrupt filesystem.

do_fiemap uses count query then allocation/fetch, no callocNULL check; count mismatch only debug and no retry/fullness proof. fiemap_count_extents0 conflates noextents and queryerror. Sparse/fragmented changed maps are weaker than a stable snapshot.

Whole btrfs helpers read: is_btrfs returns positive errno on statfs failure despite callers treating nonzero as true; source-level error/type conflation. Subvolume inode lookup and metadataUUID are explicit identity dimensions. No live Btrfs/XFS/kernel compatibility verified.

Whole ioctl/kernel headers read: per-destination SAME/DIFFERS/error/bytes fields separate, zeroed reserved ABI fields. Kernel.h READ_ONCE/WRITE_ONCE are ordinary expressions/assignment, not memory-order primitives. Call-site concurrency guarantees require examination; header names alone not proof.

Whole hash-tree and results-tree implementations/headers read. Block candidates grouped by16byte digest alone; per-file offsets unique (duplicate insert abort). Result groups keyed length+digest and members keyed filerec pointer+offset; exact repeated member insert is freed. No byte comparison in these grouping files; kernel comparison later remains separate.

Results insertion implements double-checked allocation under root mutex and per-group member mutex. dupe_extents_newNULL is not checked before insert_dupe_extents on new-group path; caller NULL checks cannot protect that internal dereference. Partial extent allocation failures in insert_result leak successful sibling allocation. Source-level OOM paths, not runtime-injected.

Range len=endoff0-startoff0+1 has no local checked arithmetic/equal-length verification against second range. Caller construction must guarantee ordered/equal nonoverflow ranges. Physical/shared lengths separate from group logical len; no automatic overlap rejection here. Need find_dupes callers before deeming externally reachable invalid ranges.

Header claims list sorting faster than tree walking are upstream historical benchmark statements, not measured rrrah optimization evidence. No speedup claimed/adopted. No implementation code copied into library.

Whole find_dupes.c/h read. compare_extents sets start before fast-forward past nonmatches. Original function control A,B,C vs A,X,C records firstA and then rangeB..C while checksum loop only visits matchingC; second range includes known mismatch at4096. Confirms false candidate span under synthetic valid4096 offsets, not hashcollision or filesystem corruption; kernelDIFFERS may reject later.

find_dupes compares block parent/digest identities, extends only contiguous offsets, currently cannot cross original physical extent boundary per sourceTODO. It loads found_extent but does not use its length locally. Range equal length/end conditions are partly derived from block_len per file, with no explicit symmetric equality check before insert_result.

Search worker always increments processed count even on DB/search failure. Source uses per-thread db handle here (unlike scanner shared static pointer observed earlier); do not assume all modules have same ownership. Search error propagation returnsvoid from worker; not a completed-success proof.

Whole dbfile.c read. Version/hash compatibility checked, cached blocksize overrides CLI but is not revalidated against bounds/nonzero. Opening named DB uses READWRITE/NOMUTEX, sets WAL and synchronousOFF, chmod0600, may unlink/recreate on compatibility mismatch. No upstream opening command executed against user data; persistence/durability not qualified by WAL alone.

Schema completed marker is files.digest nonNULL; enqueue upsert leaves digest/flagsNULL, worker hashes transaction updatesdigest+flags; next write/update run prunes unscanned NULLdigest rows. This provides explicit interrupted-scan recovery boundary, not full runtime error propagation.

Duplicate extent SQL correctly groups(digest,len), wholefiles(digest,size). GET_NONDUPE_EXTENTS instead counts digest only: original SQL in-memory fabricated same-digest/differentlength control returns no nonduplicate extent even though each(digest,len)pair unique. No actual hashcollision demonstrated.

dbfile_load_nondupe_file_extents sets output pointer then frees it on error, caller cleanup may doublefree; realloc assignment loses prior allocation on failure. dbfile_open_handle calloc unchecked; whole module has multiple resource-failure validation gaps. No real fault injection/ASAN run.
